cohort: 149 morbidly obese women who delivered either before (n=104) or after (n=45) bariatric surgery.
finding: Women who delivered after bariatric surgery experienced improved maternal outcomes (lower rates of anemia, gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and premature membrane rupture) and different neonatal outcomes (lower birth weight, but also a relatively high number of SGAs) compared to those who delivered before bariatric surgery.
birth_weight: Higher birth weight in neonates born to women before bariatric surgery (p < 0.001); relatively high number of SGAs also reported for women delivering before bariatric surgery.
gest_age: Relatively high number of small for gestational age (SGAs) cases among neonates born to women before bariatric surgery.
